solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person finding fault that could make brother lose out

indicators.note: the words that follow could be made into something else, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: fourteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fault-finder's remark could cost a brother his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person finding fault' sounds like a critic, but here it is someone whose job is tracking down faults in machinery or systems.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter diagnoses problems, literally locating the fault in equipment or an organisation.

clue.text: Not needing to offer a penny, however, doing business around East

definitions.text: Not needing to offer a penny

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'it was cold, though'

indicators.note: the word for doing business sits around the compass point, enclosing it

parts.note: trading means doing business
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A trader who never has to pay, doing deals out east.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'a penny for your thoughts': someone who can read your mind need not offer one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader knows your private musings without paying the customary penny to hear them.

clue.text: Dated shy person excluded from society

parts.note: out, as in out of date or out of fashion, means dated
to shy is to throw, and so is to cast

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned, timid person shunned by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like an adjective for a timid person; it is the verb for throwing, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a pariah, someone rejected or driven out by their community.

clue.text: Congratulating striker, dominant runner going after defence

indicators.note: the runner's word is placed after the word for defence

parts.note: in football the backs are the defenders
a lapper is a runner so far ahead as to lap others

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a striker congratulated as a strong runner gets past the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer; it is one who strikes, here with a pat on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A backslapper is an effusively hearty person who congratulates others with slaps on the back.

clue.text: Cake Charlie demolished with no end of relish

indicators.note: the name is knocked down and rebuilt, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

indicators.note: the final letter of relish is the one to be taken away

parts.note: its last letter is H

explanation.surface: Charlie wolfed a cake without any appetite left at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes H, the end of 'relish', from CHARLIE, leaving CARLIE; 'demolished' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate icing.

clue.text: Labour performer, male, dominates over Conservative

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the word for dominates stretches over the abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: rules means dominates

explanation.surface: A male Labour politician lords it over a Conservative rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' suggests the British political party; it is one of the twelve labours of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules was the mythical hero who carried out twelve labours set by King Eurystheus.

clue.text: Funny, unlike 1984

definitions.meaning: second meaning: not even, as 1984 is an even number

explanation.walkthrough: 1984 summons Orwell's novel, but it is just a number, and an even one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means peculiar and also describes integers not divisible by two.

clue.text: Raised heavy reading I have reduced, provoking strong feelings

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large, weighty book
I have shortened to the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone raising a hefty book and finding it stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' tells you to contract I HAVE to IVE, the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language is designed to arouse an emotional response rather than reasoned thought.

clue.text: Learner in RAF — he's getting unusually low rank in it

indicators.note: the letters are put together in an unusual order, rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee in the Royal Air Force is unexpectedly given a lowly post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to the RAF, which also supplies fodder letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight sergeant is a non-commissioned rank in the RAF, below the officer grades.

clue.text: Elect one still incomplete, in relation to vision

parts.note: to elect is to choose, to opt
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for still loses its last letter, left unfinished

parts.note: calm means still

explanation.surface: Choosing someone who is still not fully formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as an adverb but is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical describes anything concerning sight, the eye, or light.

clue.text: Flier making one visibly angry before election

indicators.note: the colour comes before the word for an election

parts.note: someone red in the face is plainly angry
a poll is a vote or election

explanation.surface: A candidate flushed with fury ahead of the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot or a leaflet; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redpoll is a small finch with a red crown, so a bird, which flies.

clue.text: Travel to latest part of India — that's here

definitions.text: Travel to latest part of India — that's here

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: the latest part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its final letter is A

explanation.surface: A holiday tip: head for a newly fashionable corner of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the place you go to is a part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on India's west coast, famed for beaches and its former Portuguese rule.

clue.text: Imitative behaviour, over time, likely to provoke reaction

indicators.note: the word for imitative behaviour is laid over the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: simulating means imitating or feigning

explanation.surface: Copycat conduct, repeated over time, tends to cause a response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places SIMULATING around T, the letter going in just after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stimulating excites or arouses a response, like a stimulus does.

clue.text: Practice needed for balancing acts

parts.note: suggests training for acrobats, but the acts are accounts and the practice is a profession that balances books

explanation.walkthrough: Circus balancing acts come to mind; the balance is that of a ledger, and 'practice' means a professional business.
explanation.definitionFit: This profession keeps and audits financial records, making sure the books balance.

clue.text: Empty tune by kind of jazz quartet

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: its first and last letters are T and E
trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A jazz quartet playing a hollow number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quartet' looks like the band; it is any set of four.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group or set of four things, from the Greek for four.

clue.text: Case of leaves making trains halt, ultimately

parts.note: to train is to teach

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: its last letter is T

explanation.surface: A railway story: what makes trains stop in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests departures to fit the trains; the leaves are tea leaves. 'trains' is the verb, not railway carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a wooden box in which tea was shipped, later used for moving house.

clue.text: Every year, a term of Latin

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an expression borrowed from Latin

explanation.walkthrough: 'term' hints at a school term; it is a phrase, and the phrase itself is Latin for 'by the year'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means annually, as in a salary quoted per year.

clue.text: Appeal endlessly in tests, creating precedents

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the word for tests

parts.note: exams are tests

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a plea is an appeal

explanation.surface: A lawyer appeals repeatedly during trials and sets new precedents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' could be the verb; it is the noun PLEA, which drops its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples serve as models or patterns that later cases follow, as precedents do.

clue.text: Want something heart-warming?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the saying that it makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' is the noun for a lack, not the verb; the question mark flags the proverb about being apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence means a lack of something, and the proverb says being apart makes the heart grow fonder.

clue.text: Fall or almost fall, second from front

indicators.note: the letter is taken off the front of the word

parts.note: to stumble is nearly to fall

explanation.surface: A runner trips or nearly does, just behind the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second from front' looks like a position in a race; it is S removed from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumble is a fall, especially a sudden one head over heels.

clue.text: Book that is including design for aircraft

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is takes the plan inside it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a plan is a design

explanation.surface: A book containing a design for an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is an early aeroplane with two pairs of wings, one above the other.

clue.text: Writer making change, cut one line

indicators.note: the word for change is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: pence are small change
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An author making edits, trimming a single line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author; it is an instrument that writes. 'change' is loose coins, not alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a writing implement, so it literally writes.

clue.text: Corruptly mastermind a process for producing steel shares?

indicators.note: the letters are corrupted, garbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A crooked mastermind's scheme to obtain steel company shares.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the biblical beating of swords into ploughshares, the steel shares of a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up weapons turns swords into ploughshares, so arms reduction yields steel shares.

clue.text: Dog — boxer, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small breed of dog with a wrinkled face
second meaning: short for pugilist, a fighter

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer is also a breed of dog, which tempts you into reading both halves as dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a snub-nosed toy dog breed and is slang for a prizefighter.

clue.text: Material like mustard put on Indian food

indicators.note: the eager word is put on the end of the bread

parts.note: naan, also spelt nan, is an Indian flatbread
from the phrase 'keen as mustard', meaning very eager

explanation.surface: A cook spreads mustard on Indian bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen as mustard' is a British idiom for very eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing, China.

clue.text: Legendary creature following 27's lead

indicators.note: only the letters following the opening one are kept
the lead of a word is its opening letter, the one dropped here

parts.note: the first word of 27's answer is self

explanation.surface: A mythical being imitating someone else's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is SELF-EMPLOYMENT; take what follows its lead letter S in the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small magical being of folklore, so a creature of legend.

clue.text: Is able to see you producing piece of music

parts.note: can means is able
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like see you

explanation.surface: A musician is able to meet you to perform a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see you' is a farewell; ta-ta is casual British for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition with instrumental accompaniment, often religious, in several movements.

clue.text: Kind of work that has no superior

definitions.text: Kind of work that has no superior

parts.words: Kind of work that has no superior
parts.note: sounds like praise for unbeatable work, but means work with no boss above you

explanation.walkthrough: 'has no superior' reads as 'is the best'; it literally means there is no boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Working for yourself means having no employer or manager above you.
